title: Vibrationally excited HC<SUB>3</SUB>N emission in NGC 1068: tracing the recent star formation in the starburst ring
question: Study the effects of recent massive star formation in the starburst pseudo-ring and AGN activity in the circumnuclear disc of NGC 1068 on the vibrational excitation of HC3N and heating of gas and dust.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we also made use of the HST NICMOS (NIC3) narrow-band (F187N, F190N) Pa $\alpha$ line emission image of NGC 1068 with an angular resolution of $0.26\ensuremath{''}\times0.26\ensuremath{''}$ (cite: SGB2014).

recipe.goal: Identify clumps, smooth continuum maps, and measure peak continuum fluxes and source sizes
recipe.method: Identify 15 clumps above 5 sigma in 147 GHz and 350 GHz continuum maps plus 2 Pa alpha and 2 CND positions; smooth Pa alpha and 350 GHz maps to 147 GHz resolution (0.62'' x 0.42''); measure peak continuum emission at the 147 GHz maximum; fit 2D Gaussian to 350 GHz continuum to get deconvolved surface area theta^2_350.
key_parameters: Detection threshold > 5 sigma; common smoothed beam 0.62'' x 0.42''
assumptions: 147 GHz continuum in SB pseudo-ring is dominated by optically thin free-free emission; 350 GHz continuum is dominated by dust emission

recipe.goal: Extract spectra, subtract baselines, and measure HC3N line fluxes and gas velocities
recipe.method: Extract spectra in regions of interest using MADCUBA, subtract order 0-1 polynomial baselines, identify lines, measure gas velocities from HC3N v=0 or CS, and measure integrated intensities (or 3 sigma upper limits).
key_parameters: Baseline polynomial order 0-1; upper limits at 3 sigma

recipe.goal: Estimate ZAMS stellar masses and molecular gas masses in the SB pseudo-ring
recipe.method: Calculate ionizing photon production rates Q^0 from Pa alpha and 147 GHz continuum (Eqs. 1 and 2) and convert to ZAMS stellar masses M_* (Eq. 3); calculate 350 GHz dust optical depth tau_350 (Eq. 4) and convert to gas mass M_gas using deconvolved area theta^2_350 (Eq. 5).
assumptions: T_dust = 80 K, kappa_350 = 1.9 cm^2 g^-1, dust-to-gas ratio DGR = 1/100

recipe.goal: Derive LTE excitation temperatures and HC3N column densities
recipe.method: Construct rotational diagrams (Eqs. 6-8) and fit straight lines via least squares to derive N, T_rot, and T_vib; perform LTE line profile fitting using MADCUBA SLIM tool to account for line profiles, opacity, and blending.
assumptions: LTE, optically thin for rotational diagram, electric dipole moment mu = 3.73 D

recipe.goal: Perform non-LTE radiative transfer modelling of HC3N and SED
recipe.method: Model HC3N v=0 and v7=1 line ratios (J=16-15 and J=24-23) and 350 GHz continuum SED using the non-LTE radiative transfer code from Rico-Villas et al. (2020) to derive n_H2, T_d, N(H2), N(HC3N), and X(HC3N).
key_parameters: Source size lower limit = 0.02'' (r = 0.71 pc); rotational levels up to J=45 in v=0, v7=1, v6=1
assumptions: Source size lower limit 0.021'' (1.41 pc diameter) derived assuming optically thick v7=1 J=16-15 emission

recipe.goal: Estimate IR luminosities, proto-star masses, SSC ages, and Star Formation Efficiency (SFE)
recipe.method: Compute LTE blackbody luminosity at T_vib and non-LTE SED luminosity (10-1200 um) for source size 0.021'', apply back-warming correction factor 0.2; convert luminosity to proto-star mass M_p*; estimate ages from M_p*/M_*,147 (Eq. 10) and M_*,147/M_*,Pa_alpha (Eq. 11); compute SFE from M_gas and M_*,147 (Eq. 12).
key_parameters: Back-warming correction factor = 0.2; age scale factor = 13
assumptions: Luminosity-to-mass ratio for proto-stars = 10^3 L_sun M_sun^-1; proto-star timescale ~ 10^5 yr; gas removal timescale ~ 10^7 yr

evidence.quote: For the star-forming region in the SB pseudo-ring with HC$_3$N\* emission, the LTE analysis yields a vibrational temperature ($T_\text{vib}$) between the $v=0$ and $v_7=1$ levels of $236\pm18$ K and a rotational temperature, $T_\text{rot}$, between the rotational levels in the ground state of $98\pm7$ K.

Using the ratio between the $J=16-15$ rotational transitions from the $v=0$ and $v_7=1$ states ($v_0/v_7$), we find for the SHC a dust temperature of $T_{\text{d}}=248\pm28$ K, very close to the previously derived $T_\text{vib}=236\pm18$, and a density $n_{\text{H}_2}=(5.9\pm0.2)\times10^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$.
